title: Preferred Spring Boot development environment and tool set
answer: My preferred Spring Boot development environment is IntelliJ IDEA with a supported JDK, Maven for build and dependency management, and Git for source control. I use IntelliJ's Spring-aware tooling for navigation and framework context, the integrated terminal for Java, Maven, Git, and diagnostics, and automated tests as the final verification gate. For API work I commonly use Postman, and depending on the project I may also use database tools, Docker, Jenkins or GitHub Actions, and Kubernetes. The important point is that the environment is reproducible and project-driven: the JDK baseline, Maven build, source control, and tests should behave consistently on a developer machine and in CI. For this AeroTopo learning project, IntelliJ IDEA is the only IDE used.

A Spring Boot project can behave differently when developers use different JDKs. Why should your preferred development environment begin with an explicit project SDK and language level instead of relying on a machine default?
steps.why: The IDE should match the Java baseline expected by the build and CI so local compilation, language features, and diagnostics remain predictable.
